title: Christian Faith
description: Uncompromising discipleship, total surrender, radical obedience, and hard truths for both the believer and the skeptic.
questions: Is God real? Are you 100% certain? How do you know?
To the skeptic: If you encountered undeniable evidence that Jesus Christ rose bodily from the grave, would you actually submit your life to Him, or would you still resist His authority?
What is the single biggest moral, emotional, or philosophical stumbling block keeping you from taking Christ seriously?
To the believer: How much of your faith is authentic surrender to Christ, and how much is merely comfort drawn from Christian culture and tradition?
What makes you think your faith is founded on the living Christ rather than the geographical and cultural accident of where you were born?
Like Jesus said to the rich young ruler, if He told you to sell everything you owned, give the money to the poor, and follow Him, would you do it? Would you do it right now?
Are you following Jesus for who He is, or are you following Him for the blessings, safety, and answered prayers He can give you?
When you strip away religious clichés, what do you truly believe God is like?
Jesus commanded us to love our enemies and pray for those who persecute us. Who is your greatest enemy right now, and what have you genuinely prayed for them this week?
Would you still worship and trust God if He never answered another prayer the way you wanted Him to for the rest of your life?
In what ways has your political ideology or national patriotism quietly hijacked your allegiance to the Kingdom of God?
Can a follower of Jesus participate in war, nationalism, and state violence, or does Christ's command to turn the other cheek demand radical peacemaking?
How much time do you spend seeking God in hidden, quiet prayer compared to how much time you spend talking about Him or consuming religious content?
If Jesus were to walk into your local church this Sunday looking like a homeless migrant or destitute beggar, would your congregation welcome Him or avoid Him?
In what areas of your spiritual life are you secretly proud, self-righteous, or condescending?
What is a secret compromise in your private life that you secretly hope God will overlook?
If non-Christians judged Jesus Christ solely on your words, finances, online comments, and treatment of others, what kind of Savior would they believe He is?
Why does a loving and all-powerful God allow horrific suffering and innocent children to experience agony, and does your answer genuinely satisfy a grieving soul?
Are your personal finances marked by sacrificial generosity toward the poor, or do you hoard wealth while assuming God understands your lifestyle?
What would your life look like if you actually believed that every word Jesus spoke in the Sermon on the Mount was meant to be obeyed literally?
Have you ever experienced a true 'dark night of the soul' where God felt completely absent, and what did that season teach you about your faith?
If following Christ began to cost you your career, your social standing, or your legal freedom in your country, would you stay faithful or quietly blend in?
Have you been filled with the Holy Spirit? How do you know?
How do you distinguish between the promptings of the Holy Spirit and the deceptive desires of your own ego and emotions?
Why are many secular communities often perceived as more welcoming, compassionate, and forgiving to broken people than Christian churches?
If God demanded that you give up the person, dream, or possession you cherish most on earth, could you surrender it with an open hand?
When was the last time your faith cost you something truly painful—money, reputation, comfort, or a relationship?
Do you spend more energy defending Christian dogma and winning arguments, or washing the feet of the marginalized and unloved?
Jesus said, 'Woe to you when everyone speaks well of you.' Are you compromising hard truths just to remain palatable and well-liked by society?
What is an area where modern church culture has made peace with the world's idols of consumerism, celebrity, and political power?
Is your private devotional life vibrant and hungry, or has prayer become an empty routine of guilt and religious duty?
How can a Christian reconcile living in extreme, insulated luxury while billions live in abject poverty and spiritual darkness?
Have you ever loved someone so deeply that you were willing to absorb their wrong and forgive them without demanding restitution or vindication?
What makes the gospel of Christ distinct from every other moral or philosophical system in human history?
Are you actively seeking God's will for your life, or are you making your own plans and asking God to rubber-stamp them?
When Jesus warned that many will say 'Lord, Lord' on the last day and He will reply 'I never knew you,' what gives you confidence you aren't one of them?
How do you treat people who can do absolutely nothing for your reputation, career, or social circle?
Can you truly worship a God whose judgments and commandments you do not always understand or emotionally agree with?
Do you genuinely tremble at God's holiness, or have you reduced the Creator of the cosmos into a comfortable, celestial therapist?
What is a teaching from Scripture that you quietly downplay or ignore because modern society considers it backward or offensive?
If you were put on trial tomorrow accused of being a radical disciple of Jesus Christ, would there be enough evidence in your daily life to convict you?
How does your understanding of the cross shape the way you handle unfair accusations and personal insults?
Is your evangelism driven by genuine, weeping heartbreak for lost souls, or by religious duty and tribal expansion?
Where is persistent worry exposing an underlying distrust of God in your life?
If God answered every prayer you prayed in the last seven days, would anyone's life change besides your own?
How do you honestly respond to the hypocrisies, abuses, and historic atrocities perpetrated in the name of the Christian Church?
Are you willing to be considered a fool for Christ's sake, or is human respectability an idol you refuse to smash?
What does it mean to take up your cross daily? What parts of your self-will died today?
Why do so many who claim to follow the Prince of Peace champion military might and retaliatory vengeance?
If the Holy Spirit completely withdrew from your daily life, how much of your ministry, routine, and church work would continue moving forward uninterrupted?
How do you hold the biblical tension between divine sovereignty and human moral responsibility?
Jesus wept over Jerusalem. What in your city or neighborhood breaks your heart enough to drive you to tears and sacrificial action?
How do you handle seasons when God remains completely silent despite desperate, pleading prayer?
In what ways have you made an idol out of theological correctness while neglecting love, mercy, and compassion?
If you knew with certainty that no human would ever discover your good deeds or financial gifts, would you still give as generously?
What does biblical justice require of you regarding the poor, the immigrant, the orphan, and the oppressed in your society?
Are you holding a grudge or refusing to forgive someone who deeply wounded you, while expecting God to forgive you fully?
A.W. Tozer said that men will fight for religion, write for it, die for it—anything but live for it. Are you living for Christ or fighting for an ideology?
How does your consumption of material goods differ in any measurable way from the consumer culture around you?
When Jesus spent time with prostitutes, tax collectors, and outcasts, the religious elite condemned Him. Who are the 'untouchables' you avoid today?
If salvation is entirely by grace through faith, what does a life of genuine repentance and holy fear actually look like?
How do you prepare your heart and mind for persecution, loss of goods, or martyrdom if it comes to your doorstep?
Do you view your work and career primarily as a vehicle for wealth and self-advancement, or as a holy assignment for the Kingdom of God?
What is the difference between a person who merely agrees with Christian doctrines and someone in whom Christ actually lives?
How often do you fast, and what does your relationship with fasting reveal about your appetite for God versus your appetite for physical comfort?
When you read the Beatitudes, do you see a reflection of your everyday character, or an impossible ideal you explain away?
What would happen to your faith if miraculous claims or biblical events were intellectually challenged—can your faith withstand rigorous doubt?

Elisabeth Elliot wrote: 'To be a follower of the Crucified means, sooner or later, a personal encounter with the cross. And the cross always entails loss.' When catastrophic, senseless loss enters your life, do you demand an explanation from God as a condition of your worship, or do you surrender your right to understand?
Are you willing to pour your time and heart into discipling someone who has nothing to offer you in return?
What does total submission to God's authority look like in your romantic desires, dating life, or sexuality?
If Jesus demanded that you love Him more than your father, mother, spouse, and children, what does that radical allegiance look like in practice?
Why is true Christian community often replaced by shallow surface-level friendliness and Sunday morning small talk?
When was the last time you confessed a sin directly to a brother or sister in Christ and asked them to pray for your healing?
How do you reconcile the ferocious wrath of God against sin with His infinite, tender mercy toward sinners?
What is the greatest idol currently competing with God for the supreme affection and attention of your heart?
C.S. Lewis said that the safest road to Hell is the gradual one—the gentle slope, soft underfoot. Where are you drifting downward unnoticed?
How does the reality of eternity alter the value you place on temporal promotions, applause, and retirement accounts?
Would you continue serving God faithfully if you were called to labor in complete obscurity without any earthly fruit or recognition?
In what ways do you use grace as an excuse for moral laziness and spiritual complacency?
If Jesus judged your spiritual life solely by how you talk about people behind their backs, what would His verdict be?
What does it mean that 'the love of money is the root of all kinds of evil,' and why do Christians rarely view their own greed as evil?
How do you discern whether an open door in life is God's providential leading or the enemy's comfortable distraction?
If prayer doesn't change God's immutable nature, why does He command us to pray persistently and boldly?
How does your faith compel you to stand up for the unborn, the orphan, the refugee, and the prisoner?
When you experience personal tragedy, do you run toward God in brokenness or pull away from Him in cynical resentment?
What is a Scripture passage that genuinely troubles you and forces you to confront your preconceived ideas about God?
In what specific area do you need to die to yourself right now?
Why do you think God chose the foolish, the weak, and the despised things of the world to shame the wise and the powerful?
If you had to describe your relationship with Christ using only verbs from the past 48 hours, what would they be?
How do you navigate the command to be 'in the world but not of it' without becoming self-righteous and isolationist?
Are you praying for the salvation and blessing of the political leaders and cultural figures you disagree with most?
What is the difference between true biblical joy in suffering and fake, forced spiritual positivity?

Amy Carmichael wrote, 'If I feel bitterly towards those who condemn me, as it seems to me, unjustly, forgetting that if they knew me as I know myself they would condemn me much more, then I know nothing of Calvary love.' How do you react when people criticize, slander, or treat you unfairly?
If Christ were to return right now, what would He find you doing that you would be terrified to show Him?
How does your fear of man and public opinion hold you back from bold, unashamed obedience to God?
What does it look like to love God with all your mind, and are you actively using your intellect to know Him deeper?
When people leave your presence, do they leave with an aroma of Christ, or with an impression of your cleverness and ego?
What would it take for the global Church to exhibit the radical unity, sacrifice, and power seen in the early believers?
How does your theology handle the solemn reality of eternal judgment and hell?
If your faith has never made you weep, never cost you sleep, and never caused you trouble, is it biblical faith at all?
What is an area where you know exactly what God has commanded you to do, yet you continue to procrastinate in disobedience?
Why is it so much easier to admire the saints, martyrs, and reformers than to imitate their radical surrender and prayer lives?

How many churches are in your city? How many Bibles are in your home, in your language? There are millions of people who have had zero opportunities to know Christ. Does that concern you? How does your life show it?
If you were to die today, what would people say at your memorial service? What would Christ say?
